cards.explanation: The word is astonished, and it's exactly the word Mark uses. When Jesus teaches in the synagogue in Capernaum, the people aren't just nodding politely. They're stunned, because He taught “…as one who had authority, and not as the scribes.” I get a small version of that feeling when a whole tray comes out of the oven evenly golden.

The answer is True, and the man says it loud. In the synagogue, a man with an unclean spirit cries out, “I know who You are…” and he names Jesus as the Holy One of God. He does it right there in the open, friends, for everyone to hear.

The answer is The Holy One of God. The man with the unclean spirit cries out to Jesus, “I know who You are…” and that's the title he gives Him. He also calls Him Jesus of Nazareth in the same cry. It's quite a thing to hear from that man, in that room.

The answer is that Jesus commands the spirit to be silent and come out of the man. Two commands, no waiting. Jesus says, “Be silent!” and then, “Come out of him!” He doesn't argue with the spirit or negotiate, friends. He speaks, and the spirit has to listen.

The answer is False. Mark says all the people were amazed and began to ask one another, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!” So they were talking about it, friends. And the news about Jesus spread quickly through the whole region of Galilee.

The two words are commands and obey. The amazed people say, “He commands even the unclean spirits…” and that fits what they just watched, because Jesus gave orders and the spirit came out. That's why they called it “A new teaching with authority!” The people also say the spirits “obey Him!” They saw it happen, so they didn't need much convincing. One command from Jesus, and the spirit came out.

The answer is through the whole region of Galilee. Mark says the news about Jesus spread quickly “…through the whole region of Galilee.” That's the whole region, friends, not just one town. Quickly is Mark's word for it, too.

The answer is Simon's mother-in-law, and she's the one in bed with a fever. Mark says she was sick, and they promptly told Jesus about her. This all happens at the home of Simon and Andrew. It's a quiet scene after the noise of the synagogue.

The answer is False, and fast. Mark says Simon's mother-in-law was sick in bed with a fever, “…and they promptly told Jesus about her.” Nobody sat on the news, friends. I wish my own messages got delivered that quickly.
The answer is True. Jesus goes to Simon's mother-in-law, takes her by the hand and helps her up, and “The fever left her…” It's a simple moment, friends. His hand reaches her and the fever is gone.

The word is serve. Once Jesus helps Simon's mother-in-law up, Mark says the fever left her “…and she began to serve them.” Jesus had helped her up, and then she began to serve. Mark doesn't tell us anything beyond that.

The word is town, just like Mark says. After sunset, people brought all the sick and demon-possessed to Jesus, “…and the whole town gathered at the door.” That's one doorway and a lot of neighbors. I've had a crowded kitchen, but never a crowded kitchen like that.

The answer is because they knew who He was, and that's the reason Mark gives. Jesus “…would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew who He was.” He drove out many demons that night, and He didn't let them talk. Earlier in the synagogue, one spirit had already said, “…the Holy One of God!”

The word is pray. Mark says Jesus got up early in the morning, while it was still dark, and went out to a solitary place to pray. The evening before, the whole town had gathered at the door. Mark doesn't tell us what He prayed, friends. I think it says something that He starts His morning there.

The answer is “Everyone is looking for You!” That's what Simon and his companions say when they find Jesus in the solitary place. They had gone out to look for Him. After the night before, with the whole town at the door, it's easy to see why they said it.

The answer is to go on to the neighboring towns to preach. Jesus says, “Let us go on to the neighboring towns so I can preach there as well…” Everyone was looking for Him, and His answer was to keep going, friends. He says He wants to preach in those towns as well.

The answer is True. Jesus says it Himself: “Let us go on to the neighboring towns so I can preach there as well, for that is why I have come.” He gives a clear reason and then He goes. Mark says He went throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and driving out demons.
